text:
jamie: heads-up — after the v7 API RFC landed there's still ambiguity about the response envelope change. i want to propose a lightweight translation proxy we can run at the edge to avoid breaking client-side SDKs.
nishant: +1. can you sketch the invariants it must preserve? curious about perf and failure modes.
jamie: main goals: 1) minimal latency add (<4ms p50), 2) deterministic fallthrough (if translation fails -> return v6 payload with warning header), 3) opt-in via tenant tag so we can cohort-test.
olga: also: telemetry hooks for per-tenant mapping errors and a sampling flag for full payload logging. otherwise we won't know if clients depend on the removed fields.
jamie: yep. propose an HTTP gateway that rewrites body + headers. mapping rules stored as versioned JSON blobs in k8s configmap or S3. simple rule example:
```json
{
  "map": [
    {"from": "response.user.id", "to": "userId"},
    {"from": "response.tokens.*.text", "to": "tokens.text"}
  ],
  "fallback": "passthrough",
  "warnHeader": "X-Redwood-Compat-Warn"
}
```
taylor: how do we avoid the cost of deep JSON manip per-request? we should cache compiled map functions and compile to a small AST or js function at config-change time.
nishant: agree. compile step + LRU for tenant maps. also add a circuit-breaker: after N mapping errors in 1m -> stop translating and attach header explaining the reason.
marco: what about streaming responses (chat/stream)? we can't buffer whole responses. maybe only support structural re-mapping for non-stream endpoints initially.
jamie: good call. initial rollout: only non-streaming endpoints (text generation with full response), and embeddings/rerank. streaming translation is a follow-up.
olga: rollout plan idea: 1) opt-in tenant tag, 2) small canary (5 tenants) for 24h, 3) expand to 20%, monitor mapping-error-rate and p95 latency. add automatic rollback if mapping-error-rate > 0.5% or p95 latency regresses > 15%.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for translation-proxy v0.1 to cluster "edge-us-west" (jobs/translate-proxy-canary).
nishant: what about SDKs? should we ship a client-side shim that reads X-Redwood-Compat-Warn and maps fields locally to reduce server surface?
jamie: we should, but server-side translation buys time for customers who cannot upgrade SDKs immediately. SDK shim is lower-cost long term but uptake varies.
taylor: instrumentation checklist: per-request latency, compiled-map hit/miss, mapping-errors (parse, path-not-found), fallback-count, tenant-tag. hook these into console and alerts.
jamie: owner: infra-platform (nishant + taylor). olga owns telemetry dashboard. engineering action: implement compile-and-cache, circuit-breaker, config versioning API. timeline: canary by EOW, 20% expansion next week if stable.
marco: question: legal/data residency implications if we add an edge layer for private deployments? private mode should keep translation within VPC; don't call hosted config stores unless customer opts in.
jamie: yes. private deploys: ship local config bundles and an opt-out flag for remote lookups. document in the private deployment guide.
olga: i'll draft a short RFC follow-up with rollouts and telemetry metrics. will ping infra for the canary window.
jamie: thanks all. small PRs only — keep mapping DSL tiny. we'll iterate once we see real errors. :thumbsup:
